questions.stem: What does 'Halbpension' include at a hotel?
options: Breakfast and one other main meal
Breakfast only, with no other meals
All meals and drinks during the stay
A room at half the normal price
questions.explanation: 'Halbpension' (half board) is breakfast plus lunch or, more often, dinner. Breakfast only is 'mit Frühstück', and all meals is 'Vollpension'.

questions.stem: A hotel replies: 'Leider sind wir an diesem Wochenende ausgebucht.' What does it say?
options: Prices are higher at the weekend
The hotel has no rooms free that weekend
The hotel is closed for repairs that weekend
Your booking for the weekend is confirmed
questions.explanation: 'Ausgebucht' means fully booked. 'Leider' (unfortunately) signals bad news, which rules out a confirmation.

questions.stem: Which question asks whether breakfast is included in the price?
options: Wo kann man hier gut frühstücken?
Ist das Frühstück im Preis inbegriffen?
Wann gibt es morgen früh das Frühstück?
Kann ich das Frühstück jetzt gleich bezahlen?
questions.explanation: 'Inbegriffen' means included. The other questions ask when breakfast is served, whether you can pay for it now, and where to eat breakfast.

questions.stem: At the ticket office you are told 'In Köln müssen Sie umsteigen.' What must you do?
options: Change trains in Cologne
Get off and stay in Cologne
Buy a new ticket in Cologne
Board the train at Cologne
questions.explanation: 'Umsteigen' is to change trains or buses. 'Aussteigen' is to get off and 'einsteigen' to get on.

questions.stem: Which question asks a tourist office for advice about what to do?
options: Haben Sie noch ein Zimmer mit Balkon frei?
Was können Sie uns hier besonders empfehlen?
Wie viel kostet eine Nacht im Doppelzimmer?
Wann fährt der nächste Zug nach Bonn ab?
questions.explanation: 'Empfehlen' means to recommend, so the first question seeks advice about activities. The others ask about a room price, a train time and a free room.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Nächsten Sommer reisen wir in ___ Schweiz.'?
options: der
den
das
die
questions.explanation: A few countries take an article, among them 'die Schweiz' and 'die Türkei'. Travelling into a place uses 'in' with the accusative, so 'in die Schweiz'. 'In der Schweiz' would be a location.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Im Juli fahren wir ___ Österreich.'?
options: zu
an
nach
in
questions.explanation: Countries without an article take 'nach' for travel: 'nach Österreich', 'nach Deutschland'. 'Zu' is used for people and buildings, as in 'zum Bahnhof'.

questions.stem: Which phrase completes 'Wir haben in ___ übernachtet.' ('the renovated hotel')?
options: den renovierten Hotel
dem renovierten Hotel
das renovierte Hotel
dem renovierte Hotel
questions.explanation: Staying somewhere is a location, so 'in' takes the dative: 'dem'. After 'dem' the participle used as an adjective takes the weak ending '-en'.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Der Campingplatz liegt außerhalb ___ Stadt.'?
options: die
dem
den
der
questions.explanation: 'Außerhalb' (outside) and 'innerhalb' (inside) take the genitive. The feminine genitive article is 'der'.

questions.stem: Read: 'Das Dorf ist zwar malerisch, aber im Sommer völlig überlaufen. Wer Ruhe sucht, sollte lieber im Herbst kommen.' What does the writer recommend?
options: Visiting in summer when the village looks best
Avoiding the village because it is not pretty
Staying in a quieter village in summer
Visiting in autumn to avoid the summer crowds
questions.explanation: 'Malerisch' means picturesque and 'überlaufen' overcrowded. 'Sollte lieber im Herbst kommen' is the advice: come in autumn instead.

questions.stem: What does 'Die Aussicht vom Turm lohnt sich auf jeden Fall' mean?
options: The tower is open only on some days
The view from the tower costs extra money to see
You should visit the tower at the very end
The view from the tower is definitely worth it
questions.explanation: 'Sich lohnen' means to be worth it, and 'auf jeden Fall' means definitely. 'Die Aussicht' is the view.

questions.stem: Which form completes 'Im Museum gab es leider nichts ___.' ('nothing interesting')?
options: Interessantem
Interessante
Interessanten
Interessantes
questions.explanation: After 'nichts', 'etwas' or 'viel' an adjective becomes a neuter noun: capital letter and the ending '-es'. So 'nichts Interessantes', like 'etwas Neues'.

questions.stem: Read the review: 'Die Stadtführung war spannend, der Führer kannte jede Ecke. Nur schade, dass wir so schnell durch die Altstadt gelaufen sind.' What is the reviewer's view?
options: Negative, because the old town was dull
Positive overall, though the tour moved too fast
Negative, because the guide knew little
Positive, because they had plenty of time
questions.explanation: 'Spannend' and the guide who knew 'jede Ecke' (every corner) are praise. 'Nur schade, dass ...' adds one complaint: they went through the old town too quickly.

questions.stem: Which king had Schloss Neuschwanstein built?
options: Frederick the Great of Prussia
Maximilian I of Bavaria
Wilhelm I of Prussia
Ludwig II of Bavaria
questions.explanation: King Ludwig II of Bavaria commissioned Neuschwanstein in the 19th century as a romantic retreat. Frederick the Great built Sanssouci in Potsdam.

questions.stem: What is the Zugspitze?
options: The longest river valley in Bavaria
A ski resort in the Austrian Tyrol
Germany's highest mountain, on the border with Austria
A famous Swiss railway line that crosses the high Alps
questions.explanation: The Zugspitze, near Garmisch-Partenkirchen, is Germany's highest peak at about 2,960 metres, and the Austrian border runs over it.

questions.stem: Which lake borders Germany, Austria and Switzerland?
options: der Genfer See
der Wörthersee
der Bodensee
der Chiemsee
questions.explanation: Lake Constance, 'der Bodensee', has shores in all three countries. The Chiemsee is in Bavaria, Lake Geneva lies between Switzerland and France, and the Wörthersee is in Austria.

questions.stem: What is special about Zermatt, the Swiss village below the Matterhorn?
options: It lies right on the border with Germany
It is the capital city of Switzerland
It is free of ordinary petrol and diesel cars
It can be reached only by cable car from the valley
questions.explanation: Zermatt bans ordinary combustion-engine cars, so visitors arrive by train and get around on foot or in small electric vehicles. Bern is the Swiss capital.

questions.stem: Building on Cologne Cathedral, 'der Kölner Dom', began in 1248. When was it finally completed?
questions.explanation: Work stopped for centuries in the Middle Ages and resumed in the 19th century; the cathedral was completed in 1880. It is a World Heritage site.

questions.stem: Which form completes 'Wir waren gestern im ___ Dom.' (from Köln)?
options: Kölns
Kölner
Kölnern
Kölnen
questions.explanation: Adjectives made from city names end in '-er' and never change their ending: 'im Kölner Dom', 'das Brandenburger Tor', 'Münchner Bier'.

questions.stem: Why is 'Pünktlichkeit' often stressed in guides to German etiquette?
options: Arriving early is thought to be rude by most hosts
Most meetings start ten minutes late
Guests are expected to arrive in groups
Being on time is seen as a sign of respect
questions.explanation: Punctuality matters in German-speaking countries: arriving late without warning can seem disrespectful, so people let others know if they are delayed.

questions.stem: In a busy café you want to sit at a table where someone is already seated. What do you ask?
options: Ist dieser Platz noch frei?
Wo ist hier der Ausgang?
Darf ich bitte zahlen?
Ist dieser Platz sehr teuer?
questions.explanation: 'Ist dieser Platz noch frei?' asks if the seat is free. Sharing a table with strangers in a busy café or beer garden is normal once you have asked.

questions.stem: The bill is 18,40 Euro. You hand the waiter 20 Euro and say 'Stimmt so.' What do you mean?
options: Please bring my change
I would like a receipt
Keep the change
That bill is correct
questions.explanation: 'Stimmt so' tells the waiter to keep the rest as a tip. Literally it means 'that is right', which is the trap. Germans usually tip by telling the waiter the total they want to pay.

questions.stem: The waiter asks 'Zusammen oder getrennt?' What does he want to know?
options: Whether you want to share one dessert
Whether you will pay together or separately
Whether you want to sit together or apart
Whether the meals should come together
questions.explanation: When the bill comes, the waiter asks if one person pays for all or each pays separately. Paying separately is common among friends.

questions.stem: What is usual on Sundays in Germany?
options: Rubbish is collected from every street
Schools hold their sports days
Most shops are closed all day
Shops stay open late into the night
questions.explanation: Sunday is a day of rest, and most shops are closed apart from exceptions such as bakeries for a few hours, petrol stations and shops at railway stations.

questions.stem: Around midday a colleague passes you in the office and says 'Mahlzeit!'. What is this?
options: An invitation to dinner
A toast before drinking
A wish for a good weekend
A greeting at lunchtime
questions.explanation: 'Mahlzeit' (meal time) is used as a greeting around lunchtime, especially at work. A toast is 'Prost!' or 'Zum Wohl!'.

questions.stem: What is 'der Stammtisch' in a German pub?
options: The table where the owner's family eats
A table kept for a group of regulars
The most expensive table in the room
A long table shared at a beer festival
questions.explanation: A 'Stammtisch' is a table reserved for regular guests who meet there, often weekly. It shows how a pub can give people a sense of belonging.

questions.stem: Why did the Oktoberfest begin in Munich in 1810?
options: To celebrate Bavaria becoming part of Germany
To celebrate the wedding of Crown Prince Ludwig and Princess Therese
To celebrate the end of the hop harvest in Bavaria
To mark the opening of Munich's first brewery
questions.explanation: The first Oktoberfest was a celebration of the royal wedding in October 1810, held on a meadow named after the bride, the Theresienwiese.

questions.stem: In Germany and Austria, what must a dish sold as 'Wiener Schnitzel' be made from?
options: Chicken
Beef
Veal
Pork
questions.explanation: A 'Wiener Schnitzel' must be veal. A pork version has to be called 'Schnitzel Wiener Art' (Viennese-style schnitzel).

questions.stem: Read: 'Für mich gehört das gemeinsame Abendessen zum Familienleben. Da erzählt jeder von seinem Tag, und niemand schaut aufs Handy.' What does the meal mean to the writer?
options: A time for the family to connect without distractions
A quick meal before everyone goes out again
A chance to check her phone while others talk
A formal occasion kept for special days
questions.explanation: 'Gehört zum Familienleben' shows the meal is part of family life, everyone tells of their day, and nobody looks at a phone. That is shared time without distractions.

questions.stem: What is the 'Jugendweihe'?
options: A church blessing given to babies after birth
A ceremony marking the end of Year 10
A sports award for the best young athletes
A non-religious coming-of-age ceremony at about 14
questions.explanation: The 'Jugendweihe' is a secular ceremony for young people of about 14, widespread in the former GDR and still common in eastern Germany. It is a non-religious alternative to confirmation.

questions.stem: Which church rite of passage do many Protestant young people in Germany celebrate at about 14?
options: die Erstkommunion
die Trauung
die Konfirmation
die Taufe
questions.explanation: Protestant teenagers are confirmed at about 14. 'Die Taufe' is baptism, usually as a baby; Catholic children take 'die Erstkommunion' at about nine; 'die Trauung' is a wedding ceremony.

questions.stem: At many German weddings the couple saw through a log together after the ceremony. What is this meant to show?
options: That they can work together through difficulties
That the groom is strong enough to build a house
That the bride's family has accepted the groom
That the couple plan to live in the country
questions.explanation: Sawing a log ('Baumstamm sägen') with a two-person saw needs teamwork, so it symbolises facing the problems of married life together.

questions.stem: Why do many Germans avoid wishing someone a happy birthday before the day itself?
options: Only family may say it early
It is thought to bring bad luck
It is seen as far too formal
Cards must always arrive on the day
questions.explanation: Congratulating someone early is widely thought to bring bad luck. Instead, friends often 'reinfeiern': they celebrate together until midnight and then wish them well.

questions.stem: What does the Goethe-Institut do around the world?
options: It runs Germany's embassies in other countries
It publishes Goethe's complete works
It trains teachers only inside Germany
It promotes German language and culture abroad
questions.explanation: The Goethe-Institut is Germany's cultural institute, with branches in many countries, including Australia. It runs German courses and cultural events.

questions.stem: Which English word comes from the name Friedrich Fröbel gave to his early learning centre?
options: wanderlust
zeitgeist
kindergarten
rucksack
questions.explanation: Fröbel founded the first 'Kindergarten' ('children's garden') in the 19th century. The other words are also German loans, but none comes from Fröbel.

questions.stem: Which custom did Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's German-born husband, help to make popular in Britain?
options: Sending Christmas cards
Lighting bonfires in November
Decorating a Christmas tree
Hunting for Easter eggs
questions.explanation: The decorated Christmas tree came from German tradition, and Albert's tree at Windsor helped make it fashionable in Britain. Christmas cards began in England.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way German language and culture are maintained in Australia?
options: All Australian primary schools teach German from Year 1
Australian street signs must also appear in German
Community schools teaching German to children on Saturdays
German is an official language of South Australia
questions.explanation: German community language schools, clubs and festivals keep the language alive in many Australian cities. Australia has no official second language.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Morgen nehmen wir ___ Stadtführung teil.'?
options: bei der
zu der
an der
an die
questions.explanation: 'Teilnehmen an' (to take part in) takes 'an' plus the dative: 'an der Stadtführung'. 'Teil' is the separable part and goes to the end.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Das Hotel war sehr teuer. ___ haben wir nur zwei Nächte gebucht.'?
options: Weil
Trotzdem
Deshalb
Obwohl
questions.explanation: 'Deshalb' (therefore) links a cause to its result, with the verb straight after it. 'Weil' and 'obwohl' would send the verb to the end, and 'trotzdem' (nevertheless) gives the wrong logic.

questions.stem: After a long day of sightseeing your friend says 'Ich bin fix und fertig!' How does she feel?
options: Very pleased with the day
Completely exhausted
Ready to go out again
Finished with her packing
questions.explanation: 'Fix und fertig' is an idiom for worn out. 'Fertig' alone can mean ready or finished, which makes the other readings tempting.
